newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Sanguine mood pushes Taiwan shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Sanguine mood pushes Taiwan shares to higher close.

text.p: Taiwan stocks closed higher on Thursday due to what brokers called a lack of bearish news, but minor profit-taking emerged in late trade to erode the gains.
The weighted index stayed in postive territory throughout the session and ended 36.57 points or 0.56 percent higher at 6,535.59. Turnover was an active T$51.38 billion.
Brokers attributed the rise to improving fundamentals for bread-and-butter Taiwan industrials, the government's supportive attitude and a steady inflow of foreign equity funds.
"The market is bathed in optimism," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment.
The 6,500-point level appears to have become a firm support for the index, but brokers said the market needs new momentum to breach technical and psychological resistance at 6,600.
Profit-taking pressure remained heavy as the index approached the key barrier, brokers said.
"It may take a few more sessions before the index can cross over 6,600 points," Wang said.
Plastics shares were strong, up 0.81 percent. China Petrochemical rose 80 cents or 2.75 percent to T$29.9.
But textiles encountered profit-taking to erode earlier gains. Hualon lost 10 cents or 0.4 percent to T$24.9.

Acer Sertek Co, an affiliate of computer giant Acer Inc, saw its "honeymoon" rally enter a second day after its Wednesday listing debut. As it did on Wednesday, Acer Sertek surged by the daily seven percent limit, ending at T$40.
Construction firm Hung Fu topped the losers' board, falling T$1.5 or 4.21 percent to T$34.1.
Brokers said they expected the index to waver between 6,500 and 6,600 points on Friday.
